newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bank Austria Slovak unit better in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria Slovak unit better in 1996.

text.p: Bank Austria (SR) a.s., the wholly-owned Slovak unit of Bank Austria GmbH, on Wednesday said its 1996 results exceeded expectations, and that it is looking to expand its activities this year.

Joachim Reitmeier, chairman of the subsidiary, told a news conference that the bank, in its first full year of operation, posted a preliminary operating profit of 20.14 million crowns in 1996, after an operating loss of 6.13 million in 1995.

"Despite a relatively late establishment and relatively small size of the market...we manged to turn around after a mere seven months of operation, breaking even in November," he said. The bank began operating in Slovakia in November, 1995.

The unit's preliminary balance sheet totalled 5.38 billion crowns at of the end of 1996, after 1.29 billion crowns in 1995, while the volume of extended loans, of which three- quarters were credits of up to one year, reached 1.9 billion.
"We expect similar dynamics of development this year, (and) intend to focus on country's export financing," he said.
An increase in Bank Austria (SR)'s turnover from trade financing has prompted the bank to expand to the eastern Slovak city of Kosice, where it is due to open a branch in the second half of the year.

Reitmeier noted that one of the main reasons for the unit's success in 1996 was the advantage of Bank Austria's broad network throughout Europe, including Slovakia's most important trading partner, Russia.

He said Bank Austria (SR)'s future export activities could involve the country's controversial Export and Import Bank, a state-guaranteed bank for export and import loans financing and insurance, which is expected to be approved by parliament in its upcoming session in mid-February.
In addition, Reitmeier said Bank Austria's recent approval by parliament to take a 70 percent stake in its rival Creditanstalt should ensure even greater access to markets.

"As soon as the Bank Austria and Creditanstalt merger is approved by the European Union, we will act very quickly to free cooperation or perhaps the merger (of both banks' Slovak units)," he added without giving further details.
